title: Beyond Hexagonal Boron Nitride: First-Principles Study of Pentaoctite-BN and Pop-BN Monolayers
authors: Victor M. S. da Conceição, Erika N. Lima, Roberto H. Miwa, Igor S. S. de Oliveira
abstract: We investigate two novel non-hexagonal boron nitride monolayers, pentaoctite-BN (PO-BN) and pop-BN (PP-BN), using first-principles calculations. Their structural, electronic, mechanical, vibrational, thermal, and optical properties are systematically analyzed to assess their stability and potential applications. Despite being metastable with respect to hexagonal BN, both polymorphs satisfy the criteria for dynamical, mechanical, and thermal stability, indicating that they are viable two-dimensional materials. Both systems are indirect-gap semiconductors whose electronic states near the band edges are dominated by out-of-plane pz orbitals. Their distinct pentagon-octagon ring networks also give rise to different in-plane elastic anisotropies. Many-body optical calculations reveal strong excitonic effects and pronounced polarization-dependent optical absorption, with lattice engineering shifting the optical response from the ultraviolet toward the visible and infrared regions. These findings demonstrate that engineering non-hexagonal lattice architectures provides an effective strategy for tuning the electronic and optical properties of two-dimensional BN, highlighting PO-BN and PP-BN as promising candidates for future optoelectronic and photonic applications.
summary: This theoretical study investigates two non-hexagonal boron nitride polymorphs, PO-BN and PP-BN, characterizing their stability and diverse physical properties. Using advanced first-principles methods, the authors demonstrate that these lattice modifications enable significant engineering of electronic and optical responses. This work highlights a promising pathway for developing next-generation optoelectronic materials by controlling BN's bandgap and absorption spectrum.
main_problem: To systematically analyze the structural, electronic, mechanical, vibrational, thermal, and optical properties of two novel non-hexagonal boron nitride monolayers (PO-BN and PP-BN) compared to hexagonal BN.
main_result: Both PO-BN and PP-BN are predicted to be viable 2D materials with distinct lattice architectures that allow for the tuning of electronic and optical responses across visible, near-infrared, and potentially other spectral regions via lattice engineering.
method: The study employs first-principles calculations using DFT (PBE/HSE06) for structural and electronic properties, alongside advanced methods like solving the Bethe–Salpeter equation (BSE) for optical response and AIMD for thermal stability.
model_or_system: The physical systems are PO-BN and PP-BN monolayers, which possess pentagon-octagon ring networks, contrasting with the hexagonal structure of h-BN. The calculations analyze properties derived from these distinct non-hexagonal lattice arrangements.
key_observables: Electronic band gap (indirect), in-plane elastic anisotropy ($E(	heta)$), phonon dispersion relations, excitonic absorption onset energy ($	ext{Im}(\epsilon_{xx}), 	ext{Im}(\epsilon_{yy})$).
important_parameters: Metastable relative to h-BN; lattice engineering effects; spectral tuning from UV toward visible/IR regions.
main_assumptions: The polymorphs are assumed to be stable enough for practical application despite being metastable with respect to h-BN. The analysis often assumes planar structures when calculating elastic constants.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate optimized atomic structures, strain-dependent energetics comparing the phases, band structures showing orbital character at band edges, and optical spectra demonstrating polarization-dependent excitonic absorption shifts across different wavelengths.
paper_structure: The paper follows a systematic investigation: first establishing structural/electronic stability (DFT); then analyzing mechanical/vibrational robustness (elastic constants, phonons); finally characterizing advanced properties like optical response using BSE to demonstrate spectral tunability.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of polarization-dependent excitonic effects and the ability to tune absorption into the near-IR region using purely structural modifications is highly relevant for designing novel quantum emitters or photonic components in 2D materials.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Optimized atomic structures of (a) PO-BN and (b) PP-BN monolayers, shown in top view (upper panels, unit cell outlined) and side view (lower panels). Green and silver spheres denote B and N atoms, respectively. Homonuclear B–B and N–N bonds, required to close the pentagonal rings, are visible as same-colored bonded pairs.

Figure 2: Strain-dependent energetics under biaxial tensile strain (1–10%) for h-BN, PO-BN, and PP-BN. (a) Strain energy per atom, ∆Estrain. (b) Relative stability of PO-BN and PP-BN with respect to h-BN, ∆Ephase−hex; positive values indicate h-BN remains more stable.

Figure 3: Time evolution of the energy fluctuations, ∆E(t), during 10 ps AIMD simulations at 300 K for (a) PO-BN and (b) PP-BN monolayers. The final atomic configurations after the simulations are shown in top and side views.

Figure 4: Electronic properties of PO-BN (upper panels) and PP-BN (lower panels). (a1, d1) B-pz projected and (a2, d2) N-ppz projected electronic band structures; the size of the symbols represents the orbital contribution to each electronic state. (b, e) Projected density of states (PDOS) for the B-ppz and N-ppz orbitals. (c, f) Real-space charge-density distributions associated with the conduction-band minimum (CBM) and valence-band maximum (VBM), shown in top and side views.

Figure 5: Angular dependence of the Young’s modulus, E(θ), and Poisson’s ratio, ν(θ), for Pentaoctite-BN [(a), (c)] and Pop-BN [(b), (d)]. The Young’s modulus is expressed in N/m, whereas the Poisson’s ratio is dimensionless.
